findings.problem: This diff reverts commit e11187e ("fix: use preconfigured jinja2.Environment for autoescape"), whose message states: "Starlette removed the **env_options passthrough in Jinja2Templates, breaking autoescape=True on newer versions." I verified this directly by reading the installed, lockfile-pinned package: `.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/starlette/templating.py` (starlette 0.52.1, per uv.lock) shows `Jinja2Templates.__init__(self, directory=None, *, context_processors=None, env=None)` with no `**kwargs`/`env_options` passthrough at all — `fastapi.templating.Jinja2Templates` is a direct re-export of this same class. Calling `Jinja2Templates(directory=str(TEMPLATES_DIR), autoescape=True)` therefore raises `TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'autoescape'` immediately, at module import time (this is top-level code in routes.py), crashing the whole application before any route can serve a request. Even setting the crash aside, this is a reversion of a security-hardening commit: the prior code built an explicit `jinja2.Environment(autoescape=True)` that forces autoescaping unconditionally for every template; the only way to make the new call path actually run is to drop the unsupported `autoescape=True` kwarg, at which point Starlette's internal fallback (`jinja2.select_autoescape()`, enabled extensions `html`/`htm`/`xml` by default) takes over instead — a weaker, extension-dependent guarantee rather than the explicit unconditional one the prior fix deliberately established.
findings.title: Diff reverts the prior autoescape fix, crashing the app and dropping the forced-autoescape guarantee
findings.why_it_matters: This undoes a commit that was written specifically to fix this exact crash, so the app will fail to start as soon as routes.py is imported. If the crash is instead papered over by simply removing the unsupported kwarg, the explicit, unconditional autoescape=True hardening is replaced by extension-based autoescaping that silently stops protecting any template rendered as a string or added later with a non-html/htm/xml extension, reopening the XSS exposure the original fix closed.
